system.description:
Prerequisites: Basic Auspex, Basic Presence. The ancient Toreador art of "painting souls" lets an artist capture a subject's inner nature within a work of art, music, song, or performance. Falsehood cannot be portrayed through Soul Painting, for even the artist does not initially know what the image will reveal.

To create such a portrait, the artist must study the subject for a full, uninterrupted hour (often from recalled observation, looking at the subject's aura as well as appearance and carriage), then give himself over to an enthralled creative tempest. The work must be completed in a single sitting, typically taking 10–12 hours or more depending on complexity.

System: The player rolls Manipulation + Empathy (difficulty 9). A single success captures the subject's Nature (or Path) in the work. Each additional success lets the player illustrate one of the following: Willpower, Self-Control, Conscience, Conviction, Instinct, or Courage. Anyone with Soul Painting immediately recognizes every insight portrayed; others may attempt to decode it with a Perception + Empathy or Perception + Craft roll at the Storyteller's discretion. Soul Painting does not require the artist to be otherwise skilled — a crudely executed work can still communicate the subject's personality.

MET System: The player makes a Static Social Challenge (difficulty nine Traits). If successful, the player may spend up to three Social Traits to illustrate one of the above qualities each. Kindred with Soul Painting immediately recognize every insight portrayed; a character lacking the power may need to make a Static Mental Challenge against a difficulty equal to the number of qualities imbued (one to four Traits).

Costs nine Experience Traits to learn (18 experience points in the tabletop system).
